name: Shark
description: Pursuit-optimized predator intelligence. Electromagnetic prey sensing via ampullae of Lorenzini enables detection of bioelectric fields. Hydrodynamic body form minimizes drag, embodying pursuit algorithms refined over 400 million years.

scope.definition: Minimum detectable electric field gradient (nV/cm) by shark ampullae of Lorenzini, normalized to equivalent human sensory threshold as a detection ratio.

evidence.source: Kalmijn (1971) 'The electric sense of sharks and rays', Journal of Experimental Biology 55:371-383; Kajiura & Holland (2002) electroreception in juvenile sharks.
cross_domain_examples: great white shark detects 5 nV/cm — equivalent to AA battery at 1000 km distance in seawater
ampullae of Lorenzini: 3000+ electroreceptor pores per shark, each tuned to DC-8 Hz bioelectric range
platypus bill electroreception: independently evolved vertebrate electroreception for prey detection
weakly electric fish (mormyridae): active electrolocation using self-generated fields — complementary system

scope.falsifiability: If controlled prey-detection experiments show sharks fail to locate buried flatfish producing bioelectric fields in the absence of other sensory cues, electroreception is not sufficient for cryptic prey detection.
scope.measurement_limits: Electroreception functions only in water (seawater conductivity required). Detection range limited to 0.5-1 m. Electrical noise from ocean currents can mask weak bioelectric signals.

scope.definition: Energetic efficiency of shark pursuit predation — ratio of caloric content of captured prey to total metabolic cost of hunt including search, pursuit, and capture — for white shark attacking pinnipeds.

evidence.source: Klimley et al. (2001) 'The hunting strategy of white sharks at the Farallon Islands', Marine Biology 138:25-37; Weng et al. (2007) white shark energy budget estimates.
cross_domain_examples: white shark single pinniped capture provides 50-100× resting metabolic rate for 24-48 hours
white shark strike from below minimizes escape probability — surprise attack success 0.50-0.65 on pinnipeds
orca cooperative hunting provides similar energetic return with lower individual risk

scope.falsifiability: If white shark caloric return per hunt is measured below 10:1 (energy in vs energy out) consistently, the ambush efficiency model is overstated.
scope.measurement_limits: Energetic efficiency is highly variable: failed attacks cost significant energy with zero caloric return. Strike success rate against alerted prey drops to 0.15. Deep-dive approach is the primary efficiency gain.
